Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see lost, sauce.
Failing to stand out or receive attention as a result of a larger-scale change or transformation.
Being preoccupied with one's thoughts rather than paying attention to reality.
Having happened or originated in a time so long ago that it has been completely forgotten or lost.
Lost during time travel.
Unable to be understood due to having been poorly translated.
ex: I tried reading the instruction manual but many of the steps were unfortunately lost in translation.
The message of the Japanese Prime Minister's speech was lost in translation.

senses.def: Any form of information, entertainment or other media that was once available to the public, which is now believed to be irrecoverable or otherwise unable to be consumed.
Synonym of lash (“play within a mechanism”).

A dangerous situation where the neutral wire in a split-phase power system becomes broken or disconnected, forcing all electrical current to flow directly between the two line wires and exposing loads connected between line and neutral to unstable and potentially-excessive voltages, posing a risk of equipment damage, electrical fire, or electric shock.
Not understood or appreciated by (someone).
ex: Those lessons were lost on him.

senses.def: A help desk or department in a store, mall, or other such facility where customers who have lost an item can inquire as to whether it has been found and turned in; a lost and found.
Property that is found in such a state as to make it likely that the original owner unintentionally ceased to be in possession of the property, and would be unable to locate the property.
A surface stream which flows into an underground passageway.
Carcharhinus obsoletus, a possibly extinct species of requiem shark.
A disadvantaged or marginalized person who can be "brought back into the fold" with a little effort.
A soul that is destined to go to hell; a person possessing such a soul.
One who is forlorn, who lacks direction, purpose, or motivation in life.

forms_of: lose the number of one's mess

senses.def: Writings, objects, or knowledge from the past that no longer exist.
ex: The enormous collection of manuscripts from the Library of Alexandria is lost to history.

senses.def: Of a thing, event, etc., no longer used or available; unknown to or forgotten by everyone.
Of a person, no longer existent, deceased.
ex: He was a sympathiser to the poor, the suffering, and the oppressed; and by his death, one of England’s greatest writers is lost to the world.

senses.def: Of a person, physically located in a remote place where one is unnoticed or incommunicado.
Of a person, mentally focused on one's own thoughts or feelings, or on some task, to such a degree that one is unaware of other people or of one's surroundings; unconscious.
No longer extant because it was not preserved or could not last, after a significant period of time.
ex: Many early music fanzines are now lost to time.

senses.def: Income that a plaintiff in a lawsuit would have received but for the actions of the defendant, and for which the defendant is therefore liable.

A method of casting a sculpture in which a model of the sculpture is made from wax; the model is used to make a mould; when the mould has set, the wax is made to melt and is poured away, leaving the mould ready to be used to cast the sculpture.
A period of several days in which one indulges in activities such as binge drinking, drug-taking and sex.
Destroyed or sunk, with all passengers and crew having died in the process.
An unknown world out of time, place, or both, the topic of a subgenre of fantasy or science fiction.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see lost, world.
repository in a public building where lost articles can be kept until their owners reclaim them
Synonym of lost wax.
Synonym of lost wax.
A person who is lost or abandoned.
The fact or quality of being lost.
Music of unknown origin to which no specific artists can be attributed to.
